newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT seeks know-how via China/U.S. cable project.
newsitem.headline: NTT seeks know-how via China/U.S. cable project.

text.p: TOKYO, March 31 - Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Monday that it was taking part in an international project to lay a trans-Pacific cable in order to gain the know-how it will need as a global service provider.
The $1.2 billion project, announced in Beijing on Sunday, brings together 10 companies including NTT to build an undersea telecommunications cable connecting China, Japan and the United States.
NTT said that it was participating in the project to gain experience in infrastructure-building as it prepares to expand from the domestic phone market into international services.
"It will help us acquire know-how in building long-distance undersea cables, which we are lacking," NTT vice president Mitsuhiro Takase told a news conference.
NTT also said it was considering using satellites as a vehicle for its international services, as well as fixed line options such as the undersea cable.

NTT said it had not yet decided how much money to invest in the cable project. It did not go into detail about what its specific role might be and how much of the cable's capacity would allocated to NTT.

The consortium also includes AT&T Corp, Japan's Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co, and China's telecommunications ministry. The project aims to build a 26,000 km-long network with a capacity of about one million phone lines, NTT said.
NTT will be allowed to operate as an international service provider after the law governing its operations is amended by parliament in June.
The China-Japan-U.S. undersea cable, which will be ready for service at the end of calendar 1999, will be the first such network connecting NTT lines with overseas markets.
Other members of the consortium are Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, Korea Telecommunication, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, MCI Communications Corp, BellSouth Corp's SBC unit and Sprint Corp.
Takase said this is the first step in NTT's plan to boost capacity through undersea cables and that it was also considering using communications satellites to provide services to overseas customers.
According to industry sources, NTT is likely to use satellites for services between Japan and Malaysia in the planned Malaysia Super Corridor project, in which NTT has worked as an adviser.

NTT has recently acquired business licences in France, Germany and Britain, while seeking approval in the United States and Hong Kong. NTT has said it would shortly apply for licences in the Philippines and Singapore.
